title: Can the Team Still Rely on the Storage Exception?
scenario_text: Tasman Health's privacy office must decide whether an analytics team may store a category of pseudonymized patient telemetry in the company's EU-West region. The team points to a documented precedent: exception memo EX-2023-14, approved by the Chief Privacy Officer on 2023-06-01, which granted this specific data category a standing exception to the default 'store patient data only in the region of collection' rule, on the basis that the telemetry is pseudonymized and low-risk. The privacy office pulls the current governance set. The exception was granted under the Global Data Residency Standard v2, but that Standard was replaced on 2025-04-01 by the Global Data Residency Standard v3, which states: 'This Standard supersedes all prior versions. All exceptions granted under superseded standards are rescinded as of this Standard's effective date and must be re-applied for under the new criteria.' The exception register now shows EX-2023-14 flagged as Superseded - re-application required, with no new exception granted. The analytics lead needs a decision before provisioning storage: may the team rely on EX-2023-14 to store the pseudonymized telemetry in EU-West, or must it default to region-of-collection storage because the precedent no longer applies? The privacy officer must determine whether the cited exception is current governing authority or a superseded precedent that can no longer be relied upon.
question: May the team rely on exception memo EX-2023-14 to store the pseudonymized telemetry in EU-West?
changed_fact: The status of the 2023 data-residency exception memo changes from still in force under the current policy to expressly rescinded and superseded by the 2025 Global Data Residency Standard. In the base the precedent still governs; in the variant relying on it is wrong because it has been superseded.
choices: Yes; EX-2023-14 is an active, un-rescinded exception under the current in-force Standard, so it remains valid governing authority and the team may store the telemetry in EU-West.
No; the exception has been superseded by a newer standard, so the team must default to region-of-collection storage and cannot rely on EX-2023-14.
Yes; any CPO exception, once granted, is permanent and can never be rescinded or superseded under any circumstances.
No; pseudonymized data may never be stored outside its region of collection regardless of any exception.
